definitions.gloss: retaliation; payback; tit for tat; getting even
definitions.explanation: Striking back immediately after being wronged. Implies a swift, proportional response to an offense, like hitting back right away.

examples.japanese: すぐにしっぺ{返|がえ}しを{食|く}らった。
examples.english: I got hit with retaliation right away.

examples.japanese: {悪口|わるくち}を{言|い}ったら、しっぺ{返|がえ}しにもっと{酷|ひど}いことを{言|い}われた。
examples.english: When I badmouthed him, he retaliated by saying something even worse.

examples.japanese: {関税|かんぜい}を{引|ひ}き{上|あ}げたら、{相手国|あいてこく}からしっぺ{返|がえ}しを{受|う}けた。
examples.english: When we raised tariffs, we faced retaliation from the other country.

notes:
Originally from a Zen Buddhist practice called {竹篦|しっぺい} where a master strikes a student's hand with a bamboo stick. The student would immediately strike back — hence the {返|がえ}し (returning). In modern usage, it refers to any quick, proportional retaliation. Common in both personal and international contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- しっぺ{返|がえ}しを{食|く}らう: to suffer retaliation
- しっぺ{返|がえ}しを{受|う}ける: to receive retaliation
- しっぺ{返|がえ}しに: in retaliation; as payback
- しっぺ{返|がえ}しをする: to retaliate

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {仕返|しかえ}し: revenge; retaliation — broader and more deliberate; can be planned over time
- {報復|ほうふく}: retaliation; reprisal — more formal, often used in military or diplomatic contexts
- {逆襲|ぎゃくしゅう}: counterattack — emphasizes fighting back, especially from a disadvantaged position
- {八|や}つ{当|あ}たり: venting anger on an innocent party — misdirected frustration, not proportional retaliation
